item.research_question: How to systematically document experimentally reported high-entropy alloy microstructures and metallurgy-specific features to support machine learning-based phase classification?
item.material_system: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) comprising 1362 multicomponent alloys selected through the end of August 2020, excluding glassy, amorphous, and hexagonal close-packed phases
item.processing_route: Synthesis routes, hot- or cold-working, homogenization (temperature and time), annealing (temperature and time), and quenching were extracted from peer-reviewed experimental articles
item.test_conditions: Data derived from experimental peer-reviewed research articles; no new experimental testing was performed in this data article
key_findings: The dataset contains 1422 entries with seventeen columns covering identification, composition, empirical parameters, processing, and microstructure
The final dataset includes 1362 multicomponent alloys after removing entries with missing data and eliminating glassy, amorphous, and hexagonal close-packed phases
Microstructural phases are categorized as single solid solution (FCC, BCC), dual-phase (FCC+BCC), or other intermetallic/laves/martensitic phases (Im)

Empirical design parameters calculated include density estimate, enthalpy of mixing (dHmix), entropy of mixing (dSmix), melting temperature (Tm), valence electron concentration (VEC), atomic size difference (δ), and difference in Pauling negativities (χ)
Visualization shows that solid solution phases are particularly more sensitive to empirical parameters than intermetallic (IM) phases
item.mechanism: The authors explain that the dataset serves as a systematic documentation to enable machine learning and material informatics methods to extract insights and trends not immediately available from individual studies
item.limitations: The article is limited to typical empirical parameters for succinctness, though others can be developed from alloy specifications
item.future_work: Different machine learning and material informatics computational methods can be applied to this dataset to extract insights and trends thereby advancing the real-world applications of these alloys
quotes: After removing entries missing some data and eliminating glassy, amourphous, and hexagonal close-packed phases, the as-constructed dataset is reduced to 1362 multicomponent alloys.
The visualization also shows that solid solution phases are particularly more sensitive to empirical parameters than IM phases

records.text: Paper card. Question: How to systematically document experimentally reported high-entropy alloy microstructures and metallurgy-specific features to support machine learning-based phase classification?. System: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) comprising 1362 multicomponent alloys selected through the end of August 2020, excluding glassy, amorphous, and hexagonal close-packed phases. Processing: Synthesis routes, hot- or cold-working, homogenization (temperature and time), annealing (temperature and time), and quenching were extracted from peer-reviewed experimental articles. Test conditions: Data derived from experimental peer-reviewed research articles; no new experimental testing was performed in this data article. Findings: The dataset contains 1422 entries with seventeen columns covering identification, composition, empirical parameters, processing, and microstructure; The final dataset includes 1362 multicomponent alloys after removing entries with missing data and eliminating glassy, amorphous, and hexagonal close-packed phases; Microstructural phases are categorized as single solid solution (FCC, BCC), dual-phase (FCC+BCC), or other intermetallic/laves/martensitic phases (Im); Empirical design parameters calculated include density estimate, enthalpy of mixing (dHmix), entropy of mixing (dSmix), melting temperature (Tm), valence electron concentration (VEC), atomic size difference (δ), and difference in Pauling negativities (χ); Visualization shows that solid solution phases are particularly more sensitive to empirical parameters than intermetallic (IM) phases. Mechanism: The authors explain that the dataset serves as a systematic documentation to enable machine learning and material informatics methods to extract insights and trends not immediately available from individual studies. Limitations: The article is limited to typical empirical parameters for succinctness, though others can be developed from alloy specifications. Future work: Different machine learning and material informatics computational methods can be applied to this dataset to extract insights and trends thereby advancing the real-world applications of these alloys. Quote: "After removing entries missing some data and eliminating glassy, amourphous, and hexagonal close-packed phases, the as-constructed dataset is reduced to 1362 multicomponent alloys."
